description: Atlyn Pareto helps report authors examine which categories contribute to an additive quantity, such as defect counts, complaint handling costs, or customer revenue. Bind a category and a nonnegative contribution measure to see descending bars alongside cumulative share on a separately labeled percentage axis. Choose a threshold from 1% to 100%, with 80% as a starting convention rather than a universal rule. The visual identifies the first crossing and includes equally valued contributors at that boundary. A ranked table, model-formatted native tooltips, adaptive pages, Go to rank, and Show threshold make larger category sets navigable without changing the denominator. Data scope is explicit. Report filters change the query; highlight overlays do not silently change the denominator. Segmented fetching is bounded at 100,000 categories. If completeness is not established, shares are withheld unless the author deliberately enables clearly disclosed received-subset analysis. Invalid, missing, nonfinite, and negative contributions reject the analysis rather than disappearing from the total. The visual provides native selection and context-menu integration, keyboard access, a readable table, high-contrast handling, English/French resources, and RTL presentation. Very small tiles show a compact state. Runtime rendering is local, with no telemetry, remote assets, external calculation…
